preamble.text: Historical snapshot: later evidence may be reflected in current research pages and corrections.
Deterministically compiled from canonical evidence. Importance measures impact, not truth; evidence/confidence remain separate.

blocks.text: 1. Anthropic publishes a Claude-attributed subexponential #3-SAT algorithm claim with Lean materials

Desk: reasoning_posttraining Evidence: A · credible_unconfirmed · active · importance 9/10 (Paradigm-level) Importance rationale: If correct, deterministic subexponential exact counting for fixed-width k-CNF would contradict ETH and require reassessment of many conditional lower-bound results. This score represents consequence if true, not confidence; independent review is absent and practical impact is not shown.

What changed: Anthropic contributed a version-one preprint on October 27 describing a deterministic algorithm that counts satisfying assignments for fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time, including #3-SAT, and attributes the core algorithm to an internal Claude research model. Anthropic’s official repository includes the paper and a Lean 4 formalization. Its README reports a successful local Lean build and lists only Lean’s three standard axioms for the main declarations; the repository also says Lean checks the formal statement and proof, while a human must check whether the statement matches the paper. This activation did not run the build or independently assess the proof. The README says the result is asymptotic and does not establish practical SAT performance. Why it matters: If the claimed exact-counting algorithm is correct for the stated regime, it contradicts the Exponential Time Hypothesis and would affect research that relies on ETH-based lower bounds. The consequence is substantial, but the paper is a preprint, independent mathematical review is not established, and the source explicitly disclaims practical performance implications.

Demonstrated: The Anthropic-contributed v1 paper and official formal-math ETH repository are publicly accessible. The README documents pinned Lean 4.33.1/Mathlib versions, build commands, a reported successful build, the reported standard axiom list, and a separate Comparator/nanoda check. These are source-reported repository facts; this activation did not execute the checks.

Claimed: Anthropic claims its internal Claude research model found a deterministic subexponential algorithm for exact #3-SAT counting, which refutes ETH. The paper states a 2^{O(n log log n / sqrt(log n))} time form for fixed-width counting; correctness and its precise correspondence to standard ETH remain subject to independent review.

Mechanism: The paper describes a tensor-network contraction method and derives an asymptotic subexponential bound for exact #k-SAT counting. The repository README gives a condensed tensor-contraction argument, but this activation did not inspect the full paper proof or independently derive the bound.
Strongest baseline: ETH is the standard conjecture that 3-SAT requires 2^{Ω(n)} worst-case time. The paper presents an asymptotic contradiction, not a measured comparison on practical formulas.
Regime: Fixed clause width k, exact satisfying-assignment counting, and asymptotic input size. The README explicitly says the result does not establish practical performance.

Limitations: This is an Anthropic-attributed preprint claim, not an independently accepted theorem.; The README reports a build and comparator process, but this activation did not run Lean, inspect CI logs or independently audit the proof.; Lean checks a formal statement; the repository explicitly leaves paper-to-statement correspondence to human inspection.; The source says the result is asymptotic and says nothing about solving formulas in practice.; The similar OpenAI claim is a separate event and does not corroborate Anthropic’s result.

Open evidence gaps: No independent complexity-theory review or acceptance of this paper was established in the inspected sources.; The Anthropic README says Lean checks the encoded statement but not whether it matches the paper; this activation did not inspect the full statement mapping or run the comparator.; No measured performance on practical SAT instances is reported; the repository characterizes the result as purely asymptotic.
Sources: https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00577v1 · https://github.com/anthropics/formal-math/blob/main/eth/README.md
2. China establishes National Data Group as a central enterprise focused on data-resource development and AI support

Desk: policy_geopolitics Evidence: A · strongly_supported · active · importance 6/10 (Major) Importance rationale: If it develops into a national-scale operating vehicle, a central enterprise focused on data-resource development could materially shape data availability, infrastructure and commercialization relevant to AI and multiple sectors. This score reflects possible institutional consequence; the notice establishes formation and intent only, not scale, implementation, outcomes or binding data access.

What changed: China announced the Oct 20 establishment of National Data Group Co., Ltd. in Xiongan as a central enterprise whose principal business is the development and use of data resources. The National Data Administration republished Xinhua reporting that the company is intended to help realize the value of data resources, support AI development and expand the data-industry ecosystem, working with relevant government departments, localities and industry. This documents formation and stated purposes; the inspected notice gives no registered capital, operating projects, access authority, delivered services or measured economic or AI outcomes. Why it matters: A central enterprise dedicated to data-resource development could become an important institutional route for data infrastructure and commercial use serving AI and other industries. The public notice establishes its formation and stated mission, but does not establish how much it will invest, what data or infrastructure it controls, or whether the planned coordination and services change availability or productivity.

Demonstrated: The National Data Administration republished an Xinhua report dated Oct 20, 2026 stating that National Data Group Co., Ltd. was established in Xiongan, is a central enterprise and is headquartered there. This verifies the reported formation event, not operational performance.

Claimed: The report attributes to the group an intended focus on data-resource development and utilization, data-element value realization, AI support and data-industry ecosystem growth, with cross-government and industry coordination.

Mechanism: The public report describes an enterprise vehicle with data-resource development and utilization as its principal business. It states that the company is to work under relevant departments’ guidance, coordinate with local governments and industry, share capabilities and experience, and support data-resource use, AI development and the data-industry ecosystem. These are stated organizational plans; the operating mechanism and delivered services were not inspected.

Strongest baseline: The accessible official-language baseline is the National Data Administration page republishing Xinhua’s Oct 20 report (lines 2-11). The SASAC notice search result was identified but its page timed out; no claim relying on its inaccessible text is included.

Regime: A central enterprise formation and public mission announcement in China. The inspected report provides no financial statements, capital, assets, projects, data access, service-level details, budget or outcome measurements.

Limitations: The accessible source is a National Data Administration page republishing Xinhua reporting, not a company filing with financial, governance or operational detail.; No registered capital, ownership share, initial budget, assets, staffing, data holdings or project schedule was established.; The source describes intended support for AI and data-industry development; no delivered service, data-access authority, compute capacity, customer adoption or economic outcome was measured.; Formation as a central enterprise does not by itself establish a new binding data-access requirement or the identity of entities that will receive services.

Open evidence gaps: The public formation report gives no registered capital, formal ownership or governance details, startup assets or initial operating plan.; The intended data-resource, AI and industry functions have no reported delivery, data access, project, investment or outcome evidence in the inspected formation notice.
Sources: https://www.nda.gov.cn/sjj/swdt/mtsy/1020/20261020191823470535612_pc.html
3. Heads of Security reports learned attention gates that improve prompt-injection robustness in two open-weight models

Desk: evaluation_science Evidence: A · credible_unconfirmed · active · importance 6/10 (Major) Importance rationale: If independently confirmed, a lightweight architectural defense that materially increases adaptive attack cost while preserving measured utility could change security design choices for open-weight agents. The score reflects that consequence if true; evidence is one author-reported preprint on two models and bounded attack/utility evaluations.

What changed: The preprint introduces Heads of Security (HoS), which learns small per-head attention gates to separate trusted instructions from untrusted content while allowing the model to reason over that content. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B, the authors report lower adaptive RL-Hammer attack success against HoS than against an undefended base model or SecAlign++, with means over five runs on 100 held-out InjecAgent goals where available. The official project page shows a mixed utility picture: Llama AgentDyn utility is 18.3% for HoS versus 33.7% for the base model, despite lower reported attack success, while Llama AgentDojo utility is 58.5% versus 53.7%. These remain author-reported results in two open-weight model settings, not independent replication or a deployment-safety result. A checksum-matched PyPI 0.1.0 source distribution uploaded October 8 contains package code, tests and demos for both model families; this activation inspected it but did not execute it, and PyPI reports no build provenance. Why it matters: Prompt injection remains a barrier to tool-using agents. If the reported gains replicate, a small architectural intervention could improve the security–utility trade-off without full-model fine-tuning. The authors’ own project table also shows that the trade-off varies by benchmark, including lower Llama AgentDyn utility under HoS; trust labels are externally supplied, so this is one defense primitive rather than an end-to-end security system.
Demonstrated: The arXiv v1 preprint and its stated method/results are publicly available; its reported performance has not been independently established in this activation.

Claimed: The authors report that learned per-head attention gates reduce adaptive prompt-injection attack success on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B while retaining utility on selected capability and agent benchmarks. On 100 held-out InjecAgent goals, their strongest displayed RL-Hammer attacks reached up to 10.0% ASR against HoS on GPT-OSS-20B (versus 85.2% for SecAlign and 97.2% for the undefended model) and 1.2% against HoS on Llama-3.3-70B (versus 81.6% for SecAlign and 99.4% undefended); where available, these are means over five runs. The official project table also reports uneven utility trade-offs: Llama AgentDyn utility is 18.3% with HoS versus 33.7% base alongside 1.4% ASR, while Llama AgentDojo utility is 58.5% versus 53.7% base alongside 0.9% ASR.

Mechanism: Adds learned per-head, per-channel bias terms to attention logits so each head can reduce attention to tokens assigned to untrusted sources while retaining access for other heads. It trains only 46,080 gate scalars for Llama-3.3-70B and 18,432 for GPT-OSS-20B, according to the paper.
Strongest baseline: SecAlign++ (finetuning-based) and ASIDE (architectural instruction/data separation), plus each undefended base model.

Regime: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B; RL-Hammer black-box adaptive attacks on InjecAgent with 100 held-out goals; additional white-box Claudini and static agent prompt-injection benchmarks.; the official project table reports benchmark-specific utility trade-offs, including lower Llama AgentDyn utility with HoS despite lower ASR.

Limitations: All performance figures are from one arXiv preprint and were not independently reproduced in this activation.; The authors state instruction-data separation is not end-to-end: the system does not decide which sources are trusted, and tasks may legitimately require following external instructions.; Results cover two open-weight model families and specific datasets, attack budgets, prompts, channels and scoring rules; no production deployment or broad transfer is established.; The attacker can adapt after deployment and no finite evaluation establishes security.; The authors’ project table reports an AgentDyn clean-utility trade-off for Llama-3.3-70B: 18.3% for HoS versus 33.7% for the base model, despite a lower reported attack-success rate; utility varies by benchmark.; The linked GitHub repository URL returned 404 during this check, but PyPI distributes a source package version 0.1.0 uploaded October 8, 2026. Its checksum-matched source archive contains package modules and tests; it was inspected without execution. PyPI reports no build provenance, and package availability does not establish test results or reproduce the paper evaluation.

Open evidence gaps: No independent reproduction of HoS training, RL-Hammer or Claudini results was obtained. A PyPI 0.1.0 source distribution is available and its published checksum matched, but its tests were not run and the exact revision-pinned evaluation protocol has not been independently reproduced.; The evaluation does not establish robustness in deployed agents, across trust-boundary assignments, broader tools or adaptive attacker budgets.

Sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37657 · https://huggingface.co/imperial-cpg/hos-gpt-oss-20b · https://imperial-aisp.github.io/heads_of_security/ · https://pypi.org/project/heads-of-security/0.1.0/

items: Preprint reports predictable failures in rarity- and relevance-based memory for LLM group decisions — importance 5/10 · The arXiv preprint introduces CrossProfile, a diagnostic with 60 main templates and 480 ownership variants that keeps fact wording fixed while varying which agents hold supporting, decoy and irrelevant information. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and exploratory hosted DeepSeek runs, the authors report that rarity-first and relevance-first memory heuristics can reverse performance depending on who holds decoy evidence. In the classic hidden-profile condition, relevance-first selection lowers accuracy by about 20–22 points for the two local models, and removing or randomizing holder-attribution tags raises accuracy by about 13–14 points. The study uses constructed tasks and a mechanically defined answer key; it does not estimate failure rates in deployed teams. — FCMO-54F0C40DF774

NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe with multilingual speech tasks and public model artifacts — importance 5/10 · NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe on October 28, 2026, with public model artifacts. Its model card and technical report describe an open-weight offline speech model supporting transcription in 40 languages and additional tasks including speaker attribution, translation and audio question answering. NVIDIA's launch article instead reports 5.33%; the discrepancy remains unexplained. These are company-reported results, not an independent reproduction. items: OpenAI releases country-level work-activity classifications of consumer ChatGPT use — importance 5/10 · OpenAI Economic Research released Signals v3.0, a public dataset and methodology describing consumer ChatGPT messages classified into work activities mapped to 165 O*NET Intermediate Work Activities across nearly 100 countries. Quarterly series span Q1 2025–Q3 2026. OpenAI reports that, across 74 countries observed in every quarter, the ten most common activities accounted for an average 51.1% of classified work messages in Q3 2026, down from 56.0% in Q1 2025. The dataset covers individual consumer plans, not enterprise messages or Codex; the work and activity labels are automated model classifications. The release measures message mix, not employment, task completion, productivity or labor-market effects. — FCMO-4D143C0C0A0D

EU Commission schedules special scientific-panel meeting on frontier AI risks after reported loss-of-control investigations — importance 5/10 · A European Commission press release dated 9 October 2026 announced a special meeting of the AI Act Scientific Panel on frontier AI safety and security risks. In a Spanish-language follow-up published 12 October, the Commission says the meeting addressed recent loss-of-control incidents, model monitorability and recursive self-improvement; it summarizes four recommendations, including governance of internal-model risks, stronger incident-investigation capacity, international information sharing and scrutiny of training techniques that reduce monitorability. The Commission also says it will send combined questions to developers as it investigates incidents. The sources do not identify the incidents or models, publish the questions, or establish that the recommendations became binding policy. This is a first-party account of advisory work, not independent incident verification. In an October 28 press briefing, the Commission said it had received replies to expired information-request deadlines across two AI Act RFI tracks sent to more than 30 companies and was assessing them; some deadlines were extended. The automatically generated transcript names no recipients and gives no findings. — FCMO-CA575C0CC53D
